title: Azure Network Watcher Connection Troubleshooting

controlTest.positiveScenario: Replay sample `azure:monitor:metric` events with `resource_type="microsoft.network/networkwatchers/connectionmonitors"` into `index=cloud`. Confirm UC-4.2.55 returns >=1 row and the alert fires.
controlTest.negativeScenario: Replay benign `azure:monitor:metric` traffic without `resource_type="microsoft.network/networkwatchers/connectionmonitors"`. Confirm UC-4.2.55 returns zero rows and the alert does not fire.

dataSources: `index=cloud` sourcetype=`azure:monitor:metric` collected via `Splunk_TA_microsoft-cloudservices` (Azure Monitor diagnostics); validate ingest with `| stats count by sourcetype`.
spl:
index=cloud sourcetype="azure:monitor:metric" resource_type="microsoft.network/networkwatchers/connectionmonitors"
| table _time userIdentity.arn eventName sourceIPAddress
| eval uc_marker="UC-4.2.55_azure_network_watcher_co_55"
| sort -_time
description: UC-4.2.55 — Azure Network Watcher Connection Troubleshooting: queries Microsoft Azure `azure:monitor:metric` for search criteria `resource_type="microsoft.network/networkwatchers/connectionmonitors"` and returns actor, resource, and region context for fault review and change validation.
value: On Microsoft Azure, 'Azure Network Watcher Connection Troubleshooting' highlights abnormal network flow patterns—reconnaissance, lateral movement, or blocked exfiltration that perimeter tools may not correlate across cloud segments. UC-4.2.55 drives medium-priority fault alerting before customer-impacting drift.
implementation: Configure Connection Monitor tests for critical network paths (VM-to-VM, VM-to-PaaS, on-prem-to-Azure). Collect `ChecksFailedPercent`, `RoundTripTimeMs`, and `TestResult` metrics. Alert when failed check percentage exceeds threshold or round-trip time degrades significantly. Use NSG flow logs enriched with Traffic Analytics for deeper investigation.
visualization: Line chart (check failure % by monitor), Table (failing paths), Single value (overall connectivity health).
cimSpl:
| tstats `summariesonly` avg(Performance.cpu_load_percent) as agg_value
  from datamodel=Performance where nodename=Performance.CPU
  by Performance.host span=5m
| sort - agg_value
dataModelAcceleration: Enable data model acceleration for Performance (CPU node).
knownFalsePositives: Short spikes at deploy time, autoscale thrash, or a noisy neighbor on shared hosts can look bad for a few minutes. We require the condition to last across several intervals or clear on its own before we wake someone.
detailedImplementation:
Prerequisites
• Splunk Enterprise or Splunk Cloud with search access to `index=cloud`.
• Install and configure `Splunk_TA_microsoft-cloudservices` (Azure Monitor diagnostics) with the modular input for `azure:monitor:metric`.
• Prerequisite crawl UC(s): UC-4.2.58.
• Confirm field extractions in `props.conf` for `userIdentity.arn` and related actor fields.

Step 1 — Configure data collection
Configure Connection Monitor tests for critical network paths (VM-to-VM, VM-to-PaaS, on-prem-to-Azure). Collect `ChecksFailedPercent`, `RoundTripTimeMs`, and `TestResult` metrics. Alert when failed check percentage exceeds threshold or round-trip time degrades significantly. Use NSG flow logs enriched with Traffic Analytics for deeper investigation.
Validate ingest before alerting:
```spl
index=cloud sourcetype="azure:monitor:metric" | stats count by sourcetype
```

Step 2 — Create the search and alert
```spl
index=cloud sourcetype="azure:monitor:metric" resource_type="microsoft.network/networkwatchers/connectionmonitors"
| table _time userIdentity.arn eventName sourceIPAddress
| eval uc_marker="UC-4.2.55_azure_network_watcher_co_55"
| sort -_time
```

Understanding this SPL
Scopes `azure:monitor:metric` in `index=cloud` to detect azure network watcher connection troubleshooting. Tune thresholds to your change cadence; exclude break-glass principals and sandbox accounts via a lookup.

Step 3 — Validate
Compare to the provider cloud console audit view for the same 24-hour window. Confirm row counts and `userIdentity.arn` values match the vendor console. Run `| fieldsummary` on a 1-hour sample to verify extractions.

Step 4 — Operationalize and troubleshoot
Save as `4_2_55_alert` with severity aligned to `medium` criticality. Dashboard: Line chart (check failure % by monitor), Table (failing paths), Single value (overall connectivity health)..
Failure modes: (1) no events — verify modular input/API credentials and index routing; (2) empty actor fields — upgrade `Splunk_TA_microsoft-cloudservices` (Azure Monitor diagnostics) and review alias mappings; (3) API throttling — reduce poll frequency or enable queue buffering; (4) alert fatigue — tune thresholds and document exclusions in knownFalsePositives.
grandmaExplanation: We watch cloud logs for signs of azure network watcher connection troubleshooting so your team catches problems in your online services before customers or auditors do.
